stops.note: a harbour town near Sevastopol, known to the Genoese as Cembalo; the name is often explained as Turkic balık 'fish' + yuva 'nest', though this is disputed
the Battle of Balaclava in October 1854 included the Charge of the Light Brigade; knitted head-coverings sent to freezing British troops in Crimea later took the name

current_meaning: a close-fitting woollen hood covering the head and neck
